**United Airlines Introduces New Boarding Process and Joint Business Agreement**

United Airlines has made significant changes to its boarding process and announced a joint business agreement with other airlines. Here's a summary of the news:

**New Boarding Process**

United Airlines has introduced a new boarding process that aims to reduce congestion at gates and make the boarding process more efficient. The new process involves using only two boarding lanes, instead of the previous five. The lanes will be color-coded, with lane 1 being the "blue" lane for pre-boarding and lane 2 being the "green" lane for Groups 3-5. The new process will also include a notification system that will send alerts to passengers on their mobile devices when boarding begins.

Under the new process, United's top-tier frequent flyers, active military, customers with disabilities, and families with children under 2 will board first through lane 1. Group 1 will include first- and business-class customers, as well as Platinum- and Gold-level frequent flyers. Group 2 will include Silver-level frequent flyers, certain United credit card holders, and customers who have purchased priority access. Groups 3-5 will board through lane 2, with Group 5 including most Basic Economy customers.

**Joint Business Agreement**

United Airlines has also announced a joint business agreement with Copa Airlines and Avianca, which will provide customers with more choices and benefits when traveling between the United States and 19 countries in Central and South America. The agreement will allow the airlines to share revenue, coordinate schedules, and offer more seamless service to customers.

**Benefits of the Joint Business Agreement**

The joint business agreement is expected to provide customers with many benefits, including:

* Integrated, seamless service in over 12,000 city pairs
* New nonstop routes
* Additional flights on existing routes
* Reduced travel times
* Economic benefits for consumers and communities
* Expanded codeshare flight options
* Competitive fares
* Streamlined travel experience
* Better customer service

**Implementation**

The new boarding process has been tested at several airports, including Los Angeles International Airport, and will be rolled out to all United gates starting this week. The joint business agreement is expected to be implemented in the near future, pending regulatory approval.

Overall, United Airlines' new boarding process and joint business agreement aim to improve the travel experience for customers and provide more choices and benefits when traveling between the United States and Central and South America.
